docs.text: Lab Meetings Weekly Lab Meetings Lab meetings are held in person every Monday from 10:00am-11:30am in the OPG building. These serve as a forum for lab members to present their research, discuss ongoing projects, and share updates. Attendance is expected for all lab members, and active participation is encouraged. An agenda is available on our Google Drive . Please update the agenda with your presentation title and any relevant materials. Even if you are not presenting, you can add items to the agenda for discussion. One-on-One Meetings One-on-one meetings are scheduled weekly between each lab member and Kevin. These meetings provide an opportunity to discuss individual progress, address any concerns, and set goals for the upcoming weeks. Please contact Kevin to schedule a meeting.

docs.text: Digital Research Alliance of Canada (DRAC) The Digital Research Alliance of Canada (DRAC), previously known as Compute Canada, is a national organization that provides advanced research computing (ARC) resources and services to Canadian researchers. We typically use DRAC for analysis of public datasets. Specifically, we use the nibi cluster for our work. Getting Access to DRAC and nibi Apply for a CCDB account: Instructions Kevin will need to approve your application, so please send him a message once you have submitted it. It may take a day or two for approval to be granted. Once approved, login to the CCDB portal and request access to the nibi cluster. Select Resources -> HPC -> nibi and click "Request Access". Accessing nibi Once you have access to nibi, you can connect to the cluster using SSH. The command to connect is: ssh <username>@nibi.alliancecan.ca Structure of Nibi Cluster At a high level, the nibi cluster is structured as follows: Projects : Each lab has a project directory where all members can store and access data. For the Wang Lab, this is located at /project/def-wangxk . For each project, create a subdirectory in this folder. Home Directories : Each user has a home directory where they can store personal files. This is located at /home/<username> . Scratch Directories : Each user has a scratch directory for temporary storage of files. This is located at /scratch/<username> . Files in the scratch directory are not backed up and may be deleted after a certain period of time, so it is important to move any important files to your home or project directory. Nearline : The nearline storage is a long-term storage solution for large datasets. It is located at /nearline/def-wangxk . Important Notes There is limited storage space and file quota for each user on the nibi cluster. Please be mindful of your usage and delete any unnecessary files to free up space (Use command diskusage_report to check your usage). Keep this in mind when using package managers, as they can generate lots of files. When submitting jobs to the cluster, make sure to use appropriate resource requests to avoid overloading the system. Over-requesting resources can lead to longer wait times for your job to start, while under-requesting can lead to your job being killed if it exceeds the allocated resources. Learning more about DRAC and nibi DRAC Documentation Nibi Documentation

docs.text: Overview We use a variety of resources for our work, from remote clusters to data repositories. This page provides an overview of the resources we use and how to access them. Communication Slack We use slack for communication within the lab. Currently, we are part of the BHK lab Slack workspace. Please reach out to Farnoosh to be added to the workspace. Code and Data Repositories GitHub We use GitHub to host our code. Please reach out to Farnoosh or Andrew to be added to the Wang Lab GitHub organization . We recommend that for any work done on the servers like nibi, you should use GitHub to store your code. This will make it easier to share your work with others in the lab and to keep track of changes. Lab Management Google Drive We use a shared Google Drive to store lab documents and data. Please reach out to Farnoosh to be added to the Wang Lab Google Drive. Here, you can find presentations, grants, and other documents that are relevant to the lab. Computing Resources We use both the Digital Research Alliance of Canada (DRAC) and the HPC4Health (H4H) for computing needs. Please see the following pages for more information on how to access these resources: Digital Research Alliance of Canada (DRAC) HPC4Health (H4H)

docs.text: Onboarding Welcome to the Wang lab! The following document will help you with all your onboarding needs. Important : We assume that you have completed onboarding through UHN before starting in the Wang lab. Are you a rotation student? Please note that some of the steps below may not be applicable to you. Please reach out to Kevin or Farnoosh if you have any questions. Request access to Lab Resources Farnoosh can assist you with getting access to the following resources. Please reach out to her if you need help with any of these steps. Request Google Drive Access Join our Slack Join our GitHub Organization In addition, you will need to request access to the following computing resources: Request access to DRAC Request access to H4H Meetings Attend your first lab meeting Schedule your first one-on-one meeting with Kevin Schedule an onboarding meeting with an existing lab member to go over lab policies and procedures Miscellaneous Add your information for the lab website to the lab member list in the Google Drive Familiarize yourself with DRAC and H4H computing resources. See the DRAC and H4H pages for more information.
